resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1804 is the first lighthouse (burned 1808); 1817 the second; 1874 the third; 1964 the present tower. Sources number the present tower third or fourth.

notes_for_editor: Mostly rests on Lighthouse Friends (copyrighted, paraphrased) because the Marine reports before 1900 are not in the corpus. The 1876 and 1873 report passages are quoted as reproduced by Lighthouse Friends; the 1883 report as transcribed by Islands History. W. E. Ellis 1875 matched by column position in the 1910 keepers' table (scan p.259). Disagreements: NSLPS gives early light fire 1817 and keeper 'Frederick Bray 1857'; automation 1984 (record) vs by 1987; tower 13.9 m (CCG) vs 25 ft (NSLPS). The 1883 wreck captain is Brown/Browne in sources. pointprimlighthouse.com is the PEI Point Prim, not used. The Princess Louise dead's monument is nearby but access not checked. Verifier 2026-10-27: 1910 report covers the year to 31 March 1910, so the revolving light is dated by Lighthouse Friends (1910) and the report (fiscal 1909-10), possibly 1909. NSLPS also gives the second-listed tower as c. 1875 against Lighthouse Friends 1874.
